'''Matthew Goodwin''' (born December 1981) is a British [[conservative]]<ref name=":5">{{cite AV media |title=Immigration, populism and the far right: Mehdi Hasan & Matthew Goodwin {{!}} Head to Head |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?si=4Isokbd6TZcW5jT-&v=BwB6x8CUkZA&feature=youtu.be |publisher=Al Jazeera English |date=17 October 2024 |access-date=23 February 2025 |via=YouTube}}</ref> political commentator, former [[right-wing]]  political candidate,<ref>{{cite news |last=Stavrou |first=Athena |title=Matt Goodwin unveiled as Reform UK candidate for Gorton and Denton by-election |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/reform-uk-gorton-denton-matt-goodwin-by-election-b2908567.html |work=[[The Independent]] |date=27 January 2026 |access-date=27 January 2026}}</ref> and former academic. He is known for his research on right-wing movements and [[right-wing populism in the United Kingdom]].

Initially an academic commentator on right-wing and [[far-right politics]] in the 2000s and 2010s, by the mid-2020s Goodwin was known for his espousing of strong right-wing views similar to those he had previously studied and criticised.<ref name=":6">{{Cite news |last=Boffey |first=Daniel |date=2026-01-30 |title='It's about ego': Matt Goodwin's journey from far-right expert to firebrand Reform candidate |url=https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/jan/30/matt-goodwin-academic-gb-news-presenter-reform-candidate |access-date=2026-02-12 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rubinstein |first=Samuel |date=2026-02-11 |title=Matt Goodwin's road to Reform |url=https://unherd.com/2026/02/matt-goodwins-road-to-reform/ |access-date=2026-02-12 |website=UnHerd |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Glancy |first=Josh |date=2026-01-31 |title=The reinvention of Matt Goodwin, from professor to Reform radical |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/politics/article/did-dinner-snub-light-fire-in-matt-goodwin-88rnrvkng |access-date=2026-02-12 |website=www.thetimes.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Eagleton 2023 z987" /> He is a presenter on [[GB News]],<ref name="Prospect">{{cite news |last=Bloodworth |first=James |title=Matthew Goodwin, Reform and the politics of resentment |url=https://www.prospectmagazine.co.uk/ideas/philosophy/intellectuals-and-ideas/70456/matthew-goodwin-reform-and-the-politics-of-resentment |work=[[Prospect (magazine)|Prospect]] |date=16 July 2025 |access-date=27 January 2026}}</ref> and the honorary president of [[Reform UK]]'s student wing, Students Reform. In 2026 he unsuccessfully stood for election in the constituency of [[Gorton and Denton]] in [[2026 Gorton and Denton by-election|a by-election]] following his nomination by Reform UK.<ref name="The Guardian">{{cite news |last=Walker |first=Peter |title=Reform UK accused of embracing racism over its pick for head of student organisation|url=https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2025/nov/13/reform-uk-accused-racism-student-organisation-matthew-goodwin |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=13 November 2025 |access-date=13 November 2025}}</ref>

Goodwin's most recent academic role was as a professor of politics in the School of Politics and International Relations at the [[University of Kent]], where he was employed for nine years before leaving in July 2024. He also served on the [[Social Mobility Commission]] from September 2022 to 2023. He is the author of&nbsp;two [[The Sunday Times|''Sunday Times'' Best Sellers]]: ''[[National Populism: The Revolt Against Liberal Democracy]]'' (co-authored with [[Roger Eatwell]])<ref name="openDemocracy 2019 h482">{{cite web |title=White is the new black: populism and the academic alt-right |url=https://www.opendemocracy.net/en/white-is-new-black-populism-and-academic-alt-right/ |website=[[openDemocracy]] |date=2 January 2019 |access-date=22 August 2023}}</ref> and ''[[Values, Voice and Virtue|Values, Voice and Virtue: The New British Politics]]''.<ref name="z402">{{cite journal |last1=Gilbert |first1=Jeremy |last2=Williams |first2=Alex |title=The Vices of Values: Matthew Goodwin and the Politics of Motivation |journal=The Political Quarterly |volume=96 |issue=3 |pages=504–512 |date=2025 |issn=0032-3179 |doi=10.1111/1467-923X.13555 |doi-access=free}}</ref> He is also the co-author of&nbsp;''Revolt on the Right: Explaining Support for the Radical Right in Britain'' (with [[Robert Ford (academic)|Robert Ford]]), which was long-listed for the 2015 [[Orwell Prize]].<ref name=":3">{{cite web |title=Revolt on the Right |url=https://www.orwellfoundation.com/book-title/revolt-on-the-right/ |access-date=2024-10-16 |website=Orwell Foundation}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Goodwin was born in December 1981 in [[St Albans]], [[Hertfordshire]], where he was raised by a single mother.<ref>{{cite tweet |last=Goodwin |first=Matthew |date=1 December 2025 |title=I am 44 this month. For the first time in my life I feel like I am living in a country that actually despises the hardworking British majority |user=goodwinmj |number=1995568896854704220}}</ref><ref name="Prospect"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Matthew Goodwin |url=https://londonspeakerbureau.com/speaker-profile/matthew-goodwin/ |website=London Speaker Bureau |access-date=27 January 2026 |quote=Matt was born and raised in St Albans, Hertfordshire}}</ref> His parents split when he was five years old and he has stated that "money was always a problem" in what he described as a "working-class family".<ref name="times-glancy">{{Cite web |last=Glancy |first=Josh |date=2026-01-31 |title=Did a dinner snub light the right-wing fire in Matt Goodwin? |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/politics/article/did-dinner-snub-light-fire-in-matt-goodwin-88rnrvkng |access-date=2026-01-31 |work=The Times |language=en}}</ref> Former colleagues of Goodwin have been described by ''[[The Times]]'' as "somewhat sceptical of this narrative, alleging a hint of self-fashioning", saying, "He's not working class" and "The idea he is some kind of horny-handed son of toil is ridiculous."<ref name="times-glancy"/> His father was a senior NHS executive whose roles included Chief Executive of the Greater Manchester Strategic Health Authority.<ref>{{cite web |title=Matthew Goodwin post on X |url=https://x.com/goodwinmj/status/2016633888270176282?s=46&t=EgihVtO8wyNkpnEn5YprEg |website=X |date=28 January 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Goodwin |first=Matthew |title=Out of Office, Out of Sight |url=https://www.mattgoodwin.org/p/out-of-office-out-of-sight |date=19 August 2022}}</ref><ref name="times-glancy" /> His mother worked for their local NHS health board.<ref name="times-glancy" />

In 2003, Goodwin graduated with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree in politics and [[contemporary history]] from the [[University of Salford]], at which he was offered a place through [[UCAS#Confirmation and clearing|clearing]].<ref name="times-glancy" /> He obtained a [[Master of Arts]] degree in [[political science]] from the [[University of Western Ontario]] in 2004, and completed his [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree under the supervision of [[Roger Eatwell]] at the [[University of Bath]] in 2007.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=Matthew Goodwin |url=https://theconversation.com/profiles/matthew-goodwin-98054 |website=[[The Conversation (website)|The Conversation]] |date=5 July 2013 |access-date=7 January 2021}}</ref>

==Career==

=== Academic ===
Goodwin was a [[research fellow]] at the Institute for Political and Economic Governance at the [[University of Manchester]] from 2008 to 2010 and then an [[associate professor]] of politics at the [[University of Nottingham]] from 2010 to 2015. From 2015 to 2024, he was [[Professor (highest academic rank)|professor]] of politics in the School of Politics and International Relations at the [[University of Kent]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Matthew Goodwin |publisher=[[Chatham House]] |url=https://www.chathamhouse.org/expert/professor-matthew-goodwin |date=2016 |access-date=6 October 2016}}</ref> According to journalist [[James Ball (journalist)|James Ball]], teaching at Kent involved a long commute from London for Goodwin and, around 2016, he tried to secure a professorship at London universities.<ref name="BallTNE" />

Goodwin took [[Voluntary redundancy|voluntary severance]] and left the University of Kent on 31 July 2024.<ref name="WilliamsTHE">{{cite web |last=Williams |first=Tom |title=Matthew Goodwin 'still an academic' despite leaving Kent role |url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/matthew-goodwin-still-academic-despite-leaving-kent-role |url-status=live |url-access=registration |website=[[Times Higher Education|Times Higher Education (THE)]] |date=8 August 2024 |access-date=8 August 2024 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20240808161657/https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/matthew-goodwin-still-academic-despite-leaving-kent-role |archive-date=8 August 2024}}</ref><ref name="BallTNE">{{cite news |last=Ball |first=James |title=Matt Goodwin's fall into the abyss |url=https://app.theneweuropean.co.uk/2024/08/07/matt-goodwins-fall-into-the-abyss/content.html |work=[[The New European]] |date=7 August 2024}}</ref> He said that voluntary severance "made sense for me, as someone in their forties who has done a long stint at universities. Bad actors are trying to imply that I have left because of my views on current events. That is very much not the case".<ref name="WilliamsTHE" /> His research has covered a range of topics, including Brexit, British politics, the implications of rising ethnic diversity in the West, and the future of Europe.<ref name=":4">{{cite web |title=Matthew Goodwin |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=omSh8rwAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=ao |website=[[Google Scholar|scholar.google.com]] |access-date=22 October 2024}}</ref> In 2018, Goodwin published ''[[National Populism: The Revolt Against Liberal Democracy]]'' (co-authored with [[Roger Eatwell]]), which discussed factors that contributed to [[Brexit]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Two new books explain the Brexit revolt |url=https://www.economist.com/britain/2018/11/03/two-new-books-explain-the-brexit-revolt |newspaper=[[The Economist]] |date=3 November 2018 |access-date=22 October 2024 |issn=0013-0613}}</ref>

=== Other work ===
[[File:Dr Matthew Goodwin - Chatham House 2011.jpg|thumb|Goodwin at [[Chatham House]] in 2011]]
Alongside his academic positions, Goodwin was associate fellow at [[Chatham House]] between 2010 and 2020, where he authored research reports on the rise of [[populism]],<ref>{{cite web |last=Goodwin |first=Matthew |title=Right Response: Understanding and Countering Populist Extremism in Europe |url=https://www.chathamhouse.org/sites/default/files/r0911_goodwin.pdf |publisher=Chatham House |date=September 2011 |access-date=3 February 2022}}</ref> [[Euroscepticism in the United Kingdom|Euroscepticism]] ahead of the [[2016 United Kingdom European Union membership referendum|Brexit vote]],<ref>{{cite web |last1=Goodwin |first1=Matthew |last2=Milazzo |first2=Caitlin |title=Britain, the European Union and the Referendum: What Drives Euroscepticism? |url=https://www.chathamhouse.org/sites/default/files/publications/research/20151209EuroscepticismGoodwinMilazzo.pdf |publisher=Chatham House |date=December 2015 |access-date=3 February 2022}}</ref> the different political tribes of Europe,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Raines |first1=Thomas |last2=Goodwin |first2=Matthew |last3=Cutts |first3=David |title=Europe's Political Tribes: Exploring the Diversity of Views Across the EU |url=https://www.chathamhouse.org/sites/default/files/publications/research/2017-12-01-europes-political-tribes-raines-goodwin-cutts.pdf |publisher=Chatham House |date=December 2017 |access-date=3 February 2022}}</ref> and the future of Europe.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Raines |first1=Thomas |last2=Goodwin |first2=Matthew |last3=Cutts |first3=David |title=The Future of Europe: Comparing Public and Elite Attitudes |url=https://www.chathamhouse.org/sites/default/files/publications/research/2017-06-20-future-europe-attitudes-raines-goodwin-cutts-final.pdf |publisher=Chatham House |date=June 2017 |access-date=3 February 2022}}</ref> He is a former senior fellow at the [[think tank]] [[UK in a Changing Europe]]. In 2021 he was appointed as the founding director of the Centre for UK Prosperity within the [[Legatum Institute]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Legatum Institute launches new Centre for UK Prosperity |work=[[Prosperity Institute|Legatum Institute]] |url=https://li.com/news/legatum-institute-launches-new-centre-for-uk-prosperity/ |url-status=dead |date=2020 |access-date=31 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220912183512/https://li.com/news/legatum-institute-launches-new-centre-for-uk-prosperity/ |archive-date=12 September 2022}}</ref><ref name="Bland 2023 j797">{{cite web |last=Bland |first=Archie |title=Friday briefing: Has a 'woke aristocracy' really taken control of British society? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/apr/14/first-edition-new-elite-matthew-goodwin |website=The Guardian |date=14 April 2023 |access-date=22 August 2023}}</ref> where he remains a Fellow,<ref>{{cite web |title=About Matt Goodwin |url=http://www.matthewjgoodwin.org/ |website=Matt Goodwin |access-date=4 June 2025}}</ref> leaving in 2023. In February 2026, ''The Times'' reported that Goodwin had left Legatum after the report he had been hired to work on was exposed as very poor quality. Goodwin dismissed this as "utter nonsense". Legatum confirmed that the project was abandoned due to a "wholesale re-evaluation of the methodology."<ref name=":8">{{Cite news |last=Bannerman |first=Lucy |date=20 February 2026 |title=Matt Goodwin's academic project was debunked as 'total garbage' |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/politics/article/reform-matt-goodwin-by-election-candidate-paper-cxrshwmbt |archive-url= |access-date=23 February 2026 |work=The Times}}</ref>

2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200807132243/https://freespeechunion.org/about/who-we-are/ |archive-date=7 August 2020}}</ref> a group that seeks to "counter Twitter mobs that drown |title=The Liz Truss Show review – hapless ravings from a cupboard |url=https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2025/dec/05/the-liz-truss-show-review-hapless-ravings-from-a-closet |work=The Guardian and Fridays.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gbnews.com/shows/gb-news-makes-2025-programming-announcement |title=GB News makes 2025 programming announcement |website=[[GB News]]}}</ref>

After leaving the University of Kent, Goodwin wrote non-academic books, including the [[Self-publishing|self-published]] ''Suicide of a Nation: Immigration, Islam, Identity'',<ref>{{cite magazine|last1=Merrick |first1=John |title=Matt Goodwin's intellectual suicide |url=https://www.newstatesman.com/ideas/2026/03/matt-goodwins-intellectual-suicide |access-date=31 March 2026 |magazine=New Statesman |date=24 March 2026}}</ref><ref name="SLSA">{{cite magazine |last1=Leith |first1=Sam |title=The illusion and delusion of Matt Goodwin |url=https://www.spectator.com.au/2026/03/the-illusion-and-delusion-of-matt-goodwin/ |access-date=31 March 2026 |magazine=The Spectator Australia |date=30 March 2026}}</ref> which was panned by critics, such as Ben Sixsmith, Andy Twelves and Mic Wright, for its style, lack of references and because it contained fabricated quotes (from [[Cicero]], [[Friedrich Hayek]], [[Roger Scruton]], [[Livy]], [[Noah Webster]], [[James Burnham]] and [[Walker Connor]]).<ref name="MWBT">{{cite news |last1=Wright |first1=Mic |title=MattGPT: The Sorry Tale of Matt Goodwin's AI-Assisted, Fake-Quote-Filled New Book |url=https://bylinetimes.com/2026/03/23/mattgpt-the-sorry-tale-of-matt-goodwins-ai-assisted-fake-quote-filled-new-book/ |access-date=23 March 2026 |work=[[Byline Times]] |date=23 March 2026}}</ref><ref name="SSNM">{{cite news |last1=Sheera |first1=Sophia |title=Matt Goodwin's New Anti-Immigration Book 'Based on AI Hallucinations' |url=https://novaramedia.com/2026/03/23/matt-goodwins-new-anti-immigration-book-based-on-ai-hallucinations/ |access-date=23 March 2026 |work=[[Novara Media]] |date=23 March 2026}}</ref><ref name="BSC">{{cite magazine |last1=Sixsmith |first1=Ben |title=Suicide of an author's credibility |url=https://thecritic.co.uk/suicide-of-an-authors-credibility/ |access-date=23 March 2026 |magazine=The Critic |date=23 March 2026}}</ref> Twelves and Wright speculated that Goodwin used [[generative AI]] [[chatbot]] [[ChatGPT]] to write the book, with the chatbot [[Hallucination (artificial intelligence)|hallucinating]] the quotes.<ref name="MWBT"/><ref name="BSC"/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Brawn |first1=Steph |title=Reform UK's Matt Goodwin caught out using AI in new book |url=https://www.thenational.scot/news/25959866.matt-goodwin-left-red-faced-using-ai-new-book/ |access-date=23 March 2026 |work=[[The National (Scotland)|The National]] |date=23 March 2026 |language=en}}</ref> Two of the twelve footnotes in the book contained ChatGPT source information in the references' [[URL]]s.<ref name="SSNM"/><ref name="BSC"/> The incident led to the nickname "MattGPT" for Goodwin.<ref name="SLSA"/> While Sixsmith did not think Goodwin used AI, he said the book "might as well have been" written by AI given that, in his opinion, it has been "written in the humourless and colourless rhetorical style of AI".<ref name="BSC"/> He added that ''Suicide of a Nation'' "is a very bad book" that "reads like the book of a political operator extending his CV".<ref name="BSC" /> Goodwin admitted having used AI to obtain [[data set]]s, saying he "cross-checked [them] with the original source".<ref name="MWBT"/><ref>{{Cite news |last=Devlin |first=Kate |date=23 March 2026 |title=Reform politician Matt Goodwin forced to defend his new book after using AI to help write it |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/matt-goodwin-reform-ai-chatgpt-farage-b2943916.html |access-date=26 March 2026 |work=[[The Independent]]}}</ref> Later, Twelves wrote that it appeared Goodwin's book contained fabricated reports, suggesting they had also been invented by AI, and that reports that did exist contradicted the book's thesis. He criticised Goodwin for having lost his academic rigour.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Andy |first=Twelves |date=24 March 2026 |title=Did Matthew Goodwin use AI to write his book? |url=https://spectator.com/article/did-matthew-goodwin-use-ai-to-write-his-book/ |magazine=[[The Spectator]] |access-date=31 March 2026}}</ref> [[Tim Montgomerie]], one of Goodwin's Reform UK colleagues, said Goodwin should be investigated by the party and removed from its [[Candidate#Candidates in elections|candidates]] list if it transpired he had used AI to write his book.<ref>{{cite magazine|last1=Steerpike |title=Tim Montgomerie turns on Matt Goodwin's book |url=https://spectator.com/article/tim-montgomerie-turns-on-matt-goodwins-book/ |access-date=31 March 2026 |magazine=[[The Spectator]] |date=24 March 2026}}</ref> Following a debate with Twelves on GB News, Goodwin's GB News colleagues ridiculed him, including him in a section titled "Triggered Tantrums".<ref>{{cite magazine|last1=Rats in a Sack |title=Now even Matt Goodwin's own colleagues are laughing at him |url=https://www.thenewworld.co.uk/rats-in-a-sack-now-even-matt-goodwins-own-colleagues-are-laughing-at-him/ |access-date=31 March 2026 |magazine=[[The New World (British newspaper)|The New World]] |date=30 March 2026}}</ref>

Goodwin is a visiting fellow at the [[Mathias Corvinus Collegium]], a conservative educational institution that was funded by [[Viktor Orbán]]'s Hungarian government. According to the Hungarian investigative media outlet Direkt36, these positions are paid between €5,000 and €10,000 per month. Reform has denied that he was paid €10,000 a month, though has not specified how much he was paid.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Quinn |first=Ben |date=16 April 2026 |title=Orbán's defeat threatens to halt Hungarian support of populist right |url=https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/apr/16/viktor-orban-defeat-halt-hungarian-support-populist-right |access-date=16 April 2026 |work=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Mortimer |first=Josiah |date=13 April 2026 |title=Matt Goodwin's Lucrative Hungarian Fellowship Could Be in Line for the Chop Following Orbán's Defeat |url=https://bylinetimes.com/2026/04/13/matt-goodwins-lucrative-hungarian-fellowship-could-be-in-line-for-the-chop-following-orbans-defeat/ |access-date=16 April 2026 |work=[[Byline Times]]}}</ref>

=== Reform UK candidacy ===
Goodwin is the honorary president of Reform UK's student wing, Students Reform.<ref name="The Guardian" /> On 27 January 2026, Goodwin was announced as the [[Reform UK]] candidate for the [[2026 Gorton and Denton by-election]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Reform UK on X |url=https://x.com/reformparty_uk/status/2016151139893248218?s=20 |date=27 January 2026 |access-date=31 January 2026}}</ref> His candidacy was endorsed by British far-right activist [[Tommy Robinson]]. In response to the endorsement, a Reform spokesperson said of Robinson: "We have consistently been clear on this issue. He isn't welcome in the party."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Walker |first1=Peter Senior political |title=Labour accuses Reform candidate of 'toxic politics' after Tommy Robinson endorsement |url=https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/jan/30/gorton-and-denton-labour-reform-candidate-matthew-goodwin-tommy-robinson-endorsement |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=30 January 2026}}</ref>

Goodwin was unsuccessful in his bid to be elected, finishing second to [[Hannah Spencer]] of the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]], who gained 40.6% of the vote against Goodwin's 28.7%. Labour finished in third place.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Halliday |first1=Josh |title=Green party wins Gorton and Denton byelection, pushing Labour to third place in blow to Keir Starmer |url=https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/feb/27/green-party-wins-gorton-and-denton-byelection-in-blow-to-keir-starmer |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=27 February 2026}}</ref> Following the result Goodwin said: "I think we've embarrassed Labour in one of their strongest seats. The Greens can only do this in 20–30 seats in the country. We can deliver these kinds of results everywhere."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/gorton-denton-reform-candidate-matt-33499401|title=Matt Goodwin insists 'we've embarrassed Labour' despite defeat|first=Damon|last=Wilkinson|date=27 February 2026|work=[[Manchester Evening News]]}}</ref> He subsequently wrote on X that "We are losing our country. A dangerous Muslim sectarianism has emerged. We have only one general election left to save Britain. Vote Reform every chance you get. I will continue the fight. I will always fight for you. I will stand at the next general election."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Simpson |first=Greta |date=27 February 2026 |title=Reform's Matt Goodwin and Nigel Farage blame 'woke progressives, sectarian voting and Islamists' for by-election defeat |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/reforms-matt-goodwin-nigel-farage-33499496 |access-date=28 February 2026 |work=[[Manchester Evening News]]}}</ref>

Senior figures in the party defended the decision to make Goodwin, who was seen as divisive by many, its candidate.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gross |first=Anna |date=27 February 2026 |title=Reform defends choice of Matthew Goodwin as its by-election candidate |url=https://www.ft.com/content/07ea37ba-94f4-446c-96bb-f22898dcd97e |access-date=28 February 2026 |work=[[Financial Times]]}}</ref>

== Commentary ==
Goodwin's research and writings focus on British politics, [[Radical right (Europe)|radical-right]] politics, and [[Euroscepticism]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Matthew Goodwin |url=http://www.nottingham.ac.uk/politics/people/matthew.goodwin |url-status=dead |publisher=[[School of Politics and International Relations, University of Nottingham]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120715084302/http://www.nottingham.ac.uk/politics/people/Matthew.Goodwin |archive-date=15 July 2012}}</ref> Observers have suggested that Goodwin's political views have shifted considerably rightwards over the course of his career, from being [[Centre-right politics|centre-right]] to holding [[ethnonationalist]], anti-immigration and [[right-wing populism|right-wing populist]] views by the mid-2020s, having come to resemble the views he had originally studied and criticised.<ref name=":6" /><ref name=":7" /><ref name="Eagleton 2023 z987" />

A major theme of Goodwin's work has been to explain what he calls "the realignment" of British politics that has seen the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] becoming more dependent on the liberal, metropolitan middle-class for its votes, while the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] has appealed increasingly to working-class, non-university educated voters in former Labour heartlands (the "[[Red wall (British politics)|red wall]]").<ref name="Cutts Goodwin Heath Surridge 2020 pp. 7–23">{{cite journal |last1=Cutts |first1=David |last2=Goodwin |first2=Matthew |last3=Heath |first3=Oliver |last4=Surridge |first4=Paula |title=Brexit, the 2019 General Election and the Realignment of British Politics |journal=[[The Political Quarterly]] |publisher=Wiley |volume=91 |issue=1 |pages=7–23 |year=2020 |issn=0032-3179 |s2cid=214063692 |doi=10.1111/1467-923x.12815 |doi-access=free}}</ref> Goodwin recommends that political parties "lean into" this realignment by moving "left on economics and right on culture".<ref name="Rice 2022 c973">{{cite web |last=Rice |first=Gavin |title=The daring buds of May |website=[[The Critic (modern magazine)|The Critic Magazine]] |url=https://thecritic.co.uk/the-daring-buds-of-may/ |date=31 July 2022 |access-date=21 August 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Payne |first=Sebastian |author-link=Sebastian Payne |title=Values, Voice and Virtue by Matthew Goodwin review — has the Tory party bungled the post-Brexit realignment? |work=[[The Times]] |url=https://www.thetimes.com/culture/books/article/values-voice-and-virtue-by-matthew-goodwin-review-wn5pkz030}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Garland |first=Nick |title=Nothing to fear |url=https://renewal.org.uk/nothing-to-fear/ |url-status=dead |website=[[Renewal (magazine)|Renewal]] |date=26 June 2023 |access-date=21 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230821185407/https://renewal.org.uk/nothing-to-fear/ |archive-date=21 August 2023}}</ref> On the morning after the Conservatives under [[Boris Johnson]] won the [[2019 United Kingdom general election]], Goodwin tweeted: "it is easier for the right to move left on economics than it is for the left to move right on identity & culture."<ref name="Malik 2019 d288" /> [[Kenan Malik]] wrote that this view was based on an assumption that working-class people are socially conservative, and "the trouble with this argument is that the key feature of Britain over the past half century has been not social conservatism but an extraordinary [[liberalisation]]", citing examples such as attitudes to sexuality, premarital sex, and interracial relationships.<ref name="Malik 2019 d288">{{cite web |last=Malik |first=Kenan |author-link=Kenan Malik |title=The idea that the British working class is socially conservative is a nonsense |url=http://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2019/dec/22/idea-that-the-british-working-class-is-socially-conservative-is-a-nonsense |website=The Guardian |date=22 December 2019 |access-date=21 August 2023}}</ref>

Goodwin also criticised the response of the "liberal left" following Brexit, stating: "This intolerance became most visible in the aftermath of the vote for Brexit when I watched many people on the 'liberal' left berate much of the rest of the country as an assortment of racists, bigots, gammons, and morons, all the while making it abundantly clear they had never actually met any of them." He was also critical of what he perceived as radical progressives' shift from liberalism to authoritarianism and silencing of opposing views.<ref name=":1" />{{primary source inline|date=October 2024}}

In May 2023, [[Gerry Hassan]] wrote that "Goodwin is the [[populist right]]'s academic of choice, but it seems to have escaped his notice that in the past half century [[right-wing]] Tory Governments have been in office for three-quarters of the time."<ref name=":7">{{cite web |last=Hassan |first=Gerry |author-link=Gerry Hassan |title=The UK populist right has to be defeated or democracy will be trashed |url=https://bellacaledonia.org.uk/2023/05/16/the-uk-populist-right-has-to-be-defeated-or-democracy-will-be-trashed/ |website=[[Bella Caledonia]] |date=16 May 2023 |access-date=18 August 2023 |language=en-GB}}</ref> Others have characterised Goodwin as a "populist academic",<ref name="Shaw 2023 y915">{{cite web |last=Shaw |first=Martin |title=Professors, Power and Projection: the Case of Matthew Goodwin |website=[[Byline Times]] |date=2023-04-25 | url=https://bylinetimes.com/2023/04/25/professors-power-and-projection-the-case-of-matthew-goodwin/ |access-date=2023-08-22}}</ref> stating that he turned from observer into participant, becoming an apologist for populism.<ref name="Goodwin 2020 w597">{{cite web |last=Goodwin |first=Matthew |title=How universities shut out conservative academics |url=https://unherd.com/2020/08/how-universities-shut-out-conservative-academics/ |website=[[UnHerd]] |date=3 August 2020 |access-date=21 August 2023}}</ref><ref name="Politics.co.uk 2018 c891">{{cite web |title=Going native: Populist academics normalise the anti-immigrant right |url=https://www.politics.co.uk/comment-analysis/2018/10/31/going-native-populist-academics-normalise-the-anti-immigrant-right/ |website=[[Politics.co.uk]] |date=31 October 2018 |access-date=21 August 2023}}</ref><ref name="Hassan 2023 r682">{{cite web |last=Hassan |first=Gerry |title=It's time for a long and hard look at the state of the UK's democracy |website=[[The National (Scotland)|The National]] |date=14 May 2023 |url=https://www.thenational.scot/politics/23520392.need-look-long-hard-state-uks-democracy/ |access-date=21 August 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Bloomfield |first=Jon |title=Toxic Friends? A Critique of Blue Labour |url=https://politicalquarterly.org.uk/blog/toxic-friends-a-critique-of-blue-labour/ |website=[[The Political Quarterly]] |access-date=21 August 2023}}</ref><ref name="Eagleton 2023 z987">{{cite web |last=Eagleton |first=Oliver |title=Going native |url=https://www.newstatesman.com/the-weekend-essay/2023/03/going-native |website=The New Statesman |date=25 March 2023 |access-date=21 August 2023}}</ref> James Ball argues that it was around 2016, with the [[Brexit referendum]] and Donald Trump's election as US president, that "Goodwin's public [[persona]] began to transform from that of someone explaining how to counter populist and [[far-right]] movements to someone explaining them, justifying their ends, or acting as something of an [[apologist]] for them".<ref name="BallTNE" /> 
[[File:Discussion on economics with Matt Goodwin, Angus Taylor, Maurice Glasman, Andy Aldane.jpg|thumb|Goodwin (left) on a panel at the [[Alliance for Responsible Citizenship]] in 2023.]]
Goodwin has been criticised for proposing on his blog that people who do not have children should be taxed, in the form of a "negative child benefit tax".<ref>{{cite news |last=Nicholson |first=Kate |date= 6 February 2026|title=Reform By-Election Candidate Slammed For 'Handmaid's Tale' Suggestion |url= https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/entry/reform-candidate-slammed-for-handmaids-tale-comment_uk_6985fd61e4b06f7f7bb91c85 |website= Huffpost UK |access-date= 7 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Cooke |first=Millie |date=6 February 2026 |title=Reform's by-election candidate suggested people who don't have children should pay more tax |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/reform-matt-goodwin-children-tax-gorton-denton-b2914817.html |access-date=7 February 2026 |work=The Independent}}</ref>

=== On diversity, "wokeism" and racism ===
Goodwin and his ''National Populism'' co-author Roger Eatwell, writing about the United States, have argued that political polarisation has been caused by "an increasing fixation or near-total obsession among [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]] and the liberal left with race, gender and 'diversity{{'"}}.<ref name="openDemocracy 2019 h482"/> In 2018, Goodwin, along with other commentators including [[Eric Kaufmann]], [[Claire Fox]], [[Trevor Phillips]] and [[David Aaronovitch]], was due to take part in an event titled "Is Rising Ethnic Diversity a Threat to the West?" Some researchers argued that the event would encourage "normalisation of [[far right]] ideas" and criticised the framing of the title;<ref>{{cite book |last=Smith |first=Evan |date=30 April 2020 |title=No Platform: A History of Anti-Fascism, Universities and the Limits of Free Speech |publisher=[[Routledge]] |isbn=978-1138591677 |quote=Concerned about the increasing normalisation of far right ideas, over 200 scholars wrote an open letter criticising the event}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Framing ethnic diversity as a 'threat' will normalise far-right hate, say academics |url=https://www.opendemocracy.net/en/opendemocracyuk/framing-ethnic-diversity-debate-as-about-threat-legitimises-hat-0/ |website=openDemocracy |access-date=12 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Freedland |first=Jonathan |author-link=Jonathan Freedland |title=Don't normalise the far right. But sometimes we must take it on |url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2018/oct/26/dont-normalise-far-right-sometimes-we-must-take-it-on |work=The Guardian |date=26 October 2018 |access-date=12 July 2023 |issn=0261-3077 |language=en-GB}}</ref> the debate was retitled "Immigration and Diversity Politics: A Challenge to Liberal Democracy?".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Göpffarth |first1=Julian |last2=Lorimer |first2=Marta |title=Reflections on the 'open letter' debate: a middle way to approaching the radical right? |url=https://www.opendemocracy.net/en/can-europe-make-it/reflections-on-open-letter-debate-middle-way-to-ap/ |website=openDemocracy |date=8 November 2018 |access-date=12 July 2023}}</ref>

According to Huw Davies and Sheena MacRae, Goodwin's "concerns about [[wokeism]] are a recurrent theme in his output". Goodwin has described "wokeism" as "a pseudo-religion". He has acted as an adviser to the Conservative Party and in the [[July–September 2022 Conservative Party leadership election]] supported "anti-woke campaigner" [[Kemi Badenoch]], referring to her as "one of the most interesting Conservatives in British politics for a very long time". He supported the Conservative government's [[Rwanda asylum plan]], which would entail deporting asylum seekers to Rwanda,<ref name="C. Davies MacRae 2023">{{cite journal |last1=C. Davies |first1=Huw |last2=MacRae |first2=Sheena E. |title=An anatomy of the British war on woke |journal=Race & Class |publisher=[[Sage Publishing|SAGE Publications]] |volume=65 |issue=2 |pages=3–54 |date=15 May 2023 |issn=0306-3968 |s2cid=258736793 |hdl=20.500.11820/88a2ddbe-bfd1-4c48-9a86-51aeceb41a81 |hdl-access=free |doi=10.1177/03063968231164905 |doi-access=free}}</ref> and has advised the party to raise "the salience of cultural issues". Kenan Malik argues that Goodwin now advocates a politics that a decade earlier he would have described as "toxic".<ref>{{cite news |last=Malik |first=Kenan |title=This obsession with a 'new elite' hides the real roots of power |url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2023/apr/16/this-obsession-with-new-elite-hides-real-roots-of-power |work=The Guardian |date=16 April 2023 |access-date=25 August 2023}}</ref>

In 2021, when the [[Commission on Race and Ethnic Disparities]], commissioned by [[Boris Johnson]] and chaired by [[Tony Sewell]], argued that [[structural racism]] did not exist in the UK, Goodwin said this "dismantles the woke mob's central claim that we are living in a fundamentally racist society".<ref name="C. Davies MacRae 2023" /> Goodwin has also highlighted various instances of public funding for initiatives that he views as symptomatic of this cultural shift.<ref>{{cite web |first=Matt |last=Goodwin |title=Ten CRAZY things YOU are paying for right now |url=https://www.mattgoodwin.org/p/ten-crazy-things-you-are-paying-for |website=www.mattgoodwin.org |date=29 August 2024 |access-date=16 October 2024}}</ref>

===National Conservatism and UK riots===
Goodwin spoke at the 2023 [[National Conservatism Conference]],<ref name="Lloyd">{{cite web |last=Lloyd |first=Will |date=2023-05-24 |title=The Tory crack-up |url=https://www.newstatesman.com/long-reads/2023/05/national-conservatism-tories-future-conferences |access-date=2023-08-18 |website=The New Statesman |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Geoghegan |first=Peter |date=2023-06-01 |title=Peter Geoghegan · Short Cuts: At NatCon London · LRB 1 June 2023 |volume=45 |work=[[London Review of Books]] |issue=11 |url=https://www.lrb.co.uk/the-paper/v45/n11/peter-geoghegan/short-cuts |access-date=2023-08-18 |issn=0260-9592}}</ref> where he described the Conservative Party as being in a "prolonged death spiral".<ref name="Beckett">{{cite news |last=Beckett |first=Andy |title=I went to the NatCon conference expecting sinister exuberance. But all I found was doom and gloom |url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2023/may/19/national-conservatism-conference-leftwing-dark-age |work=The Guardian |date=19 May 2023 |access-date=18 August 2023 |issn=0261-3077 |language=en-GB}}</ref> Goodwin told [[CNN]] that conservatives needed to "decide who they are and what they want to be".<ref>{{cite web |last=McGee |first=Luke |title=Why are some British Conservatives behaving like the next election is already lost? |url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/05/18/uk/uk-conservatives-intl-cmd-gbr/index.html |work=[[CNN]] |date=18 May 2023 |access-date=18 August 2023}}</ref> For ''[[The Atlantic]]'', [[Helen Lewis (journalist)|Helen Lewis]] wrote that Goodwin gave "a typically doomy speech", which "segued into 10 minutes of pure populist beat poetry".<ref name="Lewis">{{cite web |last=Lewis |first=Helen |title=Why So Many Conservatives Feel Like Losers |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/ideas/archive/2023/05/national-conservative-conference-london-brexit/674095/ |website=[[The Atlantic]] |date=18 May 2023 |access-date=18 August 2023}}</ref> David Aaronovitch described Goodwin's speech as one of the two most "politically coherent" of the conference, calling him "the politics professor turned political [[entrepreneur]]".<ref>{{cite web |last=Aaronovitch |first=David |author-link=David Aaronovitch |title=Flag, faith and failure: three days with the National Conservatives |url=https://www.prospectmagazine.co.uk/politics/61787/david-aaronovitch-national-conservatism-conference-london |website=[[Prospect (magazine)|Prospect]] |access-date=18 August 2023}}</ref> Goodwin has responded to such criticisms in his writings, including in his articles "What Happened To Me?"<ref name=":1">{{cite web |last=Goodwin |first=Matt |title=What Happened To Me? |url=https://www.mattgoodwin.org/p/what-happened-to-me |website=www.mattgoodwin.org |date=24 October 2023 |access-date=16 October 2024}}</ref> and "Have I 'radicalised'?".<ref name=":2">{{cite web |title=Have I 'radicalised'? |url=https://www.mattgoodwin.org/p/have-i-radicalised |website=www.mattgoodwin.org |date=21 August 2024 |access-date=16 October 2024}}</ref> Explaining his decision to participate in the conference, Goodwin wrote: "I'm not a member of the Conservative Party. And unless something changes I don't currently plan on voting Conservative at the next election." He explained that his decision was because "one of the most interesting and important debates in politics right now is where conservatism goes next – not only here in Britain but globally."<ref name="Goodwin 2023 s718">{{cite web |last=Goodwin |first=Matt |title=Matt Goodwin: The revolution of liberal economics and woke cultural extremism has failed and left Britain broken |url=https://www.newsletter.co.uk/news/opinion/matt-goodwin-the-revolution-of-liberal-economics-and-radical-cultural-woke-extremism-has-failed-and-left-britain-broken-and-bewildered-4160873 |website=[[News Letter|Belfast News Letter]] |date=28 May 2023 |access-date=21 August 2023}}</ref>

During the [[2024 United Kingdom riots]] that followed the [[2024 Southport stabbing]], Goodwin criticised commentators who labelled the groups engaged in the violence as "far right", writing on X that there had been a "concerted & most likely coordinated effort by the elite class to inflate 'far right' to stigmatise & silence millions of ordinary people who object to mass immigration and its effects". Goodwin praised Hungary under prime minister [[Viktor Orbán]], which he described as having "no crime", "no homeless people", "no riots" and "no unrest". Conservative commentator [[Tim Montgomerie]] called Goodwin's posts "incendiary",<ref name="WilliamsTHE" /> and [[ITV News]]'s [[Joel Hills]] asked: "Matt, are you still at the University of Kent? I ask because it's so hard to imagine a serious academic publishing something like this."<ref name="WilliamsTHE" /> [[Robert Ford (academic)|Robert Ford]], with whom Goodwin wrote ''Revolt on the Right'' in 2014, had by August 2024 "ended contact with Goodwin", saying "I tried for several years to reason with him on this but to no avail. Once I could see where this was heading I cut ties and became a more public critic".<ref name="BallTNE" />

Goodwin maintains that [[Modern immigration to the United Kingdom|immigration to the UK]] constitutes an "[[Immigrant invasion|invasion]]". In a 2024 debate on immigration with [[Al Jazeera Media Network|Al Jazeera]]'s [[Mehdi Hasan]], Hasan remarked that Goodwin has "[[wikt:go native|gone native]]".<ref name=":5"/>{{primary source inline|date=February 2026}} After the [[2025 Cambridgeshire train stabbing]] was reported in the news, Goodwin posted on X that "mass uncontrolled immigration" was to blame. When someone responded that the suspect, Anthony Williams, was born in the UK, Goodwin replied "So were all of the 7/7 bombers. It takes more than a piece of paper to make somebody 'British{{'"}}. He was subsequently accused by the Liberal Democrats' home affairs spokesperson, [[Max Wilkinson]], of using racist rhetoric. Goodwin responded by stating: "What I said isn't racist. They devalue the term by saying this."<ref name="The Guardian" />

===Political predictions===
On 27 May 2017, Goodwin predicted that the Labour Party would not reach 38 per cent of the vote in the [[2017 United Kingdom general election]] and said he would eat his book if they did.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/GoodwinMJ/status/868562780990959621|title=Matt Goodwin on X}}</ref> As the party won 40.0% of the popular vote, Goodwin chewed one page out of his book, live on [[Sky News]], on 10 June 2017.<ref>{{cite news |author=Media Mole |title=Watch: Politics expert Matthew Goodwin eats his own book on live TV after underestimating Labour |url=http://www.newstatesman.com/politics/june2017/2017/06/watch-politics-expert-matthew-goodwin-eats-his-own-book-live-tv-after |work=The New Statesman |location=London |date=11 June 2017}}</ref>

In March 2024, Goodwin wrote in ''[[The Sun (United Kingdom)|The Sun]]'': "Eight years ago I did some political fortune-telling that led to people thinking I was insane. I was one of only a few analysts who predicted that not only would Britain vote to leave the EU but also that America would elect President Donald Trump."<ref name="BallTNE"/> Will Jennings of the University of Southampton said that when speaking at an event at the London School of Economics on the day of the [[Brexit referendum]], Goodwin actually predicted a two-point Remain win.<ref name="BallTNE"/>

While Goodwin gave Trump a better chance of winning in the [[2016 US presidential election]] than some pundits, he nonetheless wrote that Trump "would most likely fail".<ref name="BallTNE"/> Goodwin also incorrectly predicted that Trump would win the 2020 election.<ref name="BallTNE"/>

== Personal life ==
Goodwin lives in [[Hitchin]], [[Hertfordshire]].<ref name="Prospect"/><ref>{{cite web |last1=O’Grady |first1=Sean |title=Is Matthew Goodwin too rabid even for Reform? |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/voices/matthew-goodwin-re |work=[[The Independent]] |access-date=7 February 2026 |date=6 February 2026}}</ref><ref name="G&D SOPN">{{cite web |last1=Stannard |first1=Tom |title=Statement of persons nominated: Gorton and Denton by-election |url=https://www.manchester.gov.uk/download/downloads/id/30373/statement_of_persons_nominated_and_notice_of_poll_for_the_february_2026_gorton_and_denton_by_election.pdf |publisher=[[Manchester City Council]] |access-date=7 February 2026 |format=PDF |date=3 February 2026}}</ref> He was married to Fiona McAdoo from 2016 to 2026, and they have one daughter together.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jones |first=Ros Wynne |date=2026-02-20 |title=Reform star's grim views in full - Muslim immigration ban to deportation horror |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/uk-news/reform-candidate-matthew-goodwins-horror-36756182 |access-date=2026-02-23 |website=Daily Mirror |language=en}}</ref>{{better source needed|reason=tabloid|date=April 2026}} They separated in 2023. His current partner is Eilidh Hargreaves, a journalist at ''[[Tatler]]'', whom he met at the 2025 [[Spectator Awards]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Leake |first=Natasha |date=22 February 2026 |title=Reform's Matthew Goodwin: 'I had a swastika put on my door for having Right-wing views' |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2026/02/22/reform-matthew-goodwin-interview/ |access-date=23 February 2026 |work=The Telegraph}}</ref>

==Honours==
In 2014, aged 33, Goodwin was awarded the [[Richard Rose (political scientist)|Richard Rose]] Prize by the [[Political Studies Association]], which is given to one early-career academic each year for their contribution to research.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.psa.ac.uk/events/conference-highlights-2014|title=Conference Highlights 2014|publisher=[[Political Studies Association]]}}</ref> The award was made at the organisation's conference on 14–16 April<ref>{{cite web |url= https://socialhistoryportal.org/news/articles/307909|title=UK Political Studies Association Conference Panel on Anarchism and Radical Democracy|publisher=[[Social History Portal]]}}</ref> and Goodwin was appointed their director on 27 June, resigning on 24 June 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/officers/aEk9FwJ4Her0vAgrISJWaDxLeZE/appointments|title=Matthew GOODWIN personal appointments|publisher=[[Companies House]]|website=[[GOV.UK]] |access-date=25 February 2026}}</ref>{{primary source inline|date=February 2026}} He co-authored the book ''Revolt on the Right: Explaining Support for the Radical Right in Britain'', which was long-listed for the 2015 [[Orwell Prize]].<ref name=":3"/>
